chunks: As for what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and Umm Ismāʿīl was with him. He had intercourse with a slave-girl of his, then instructed her, so she washed her body and left her head. He said to her, “When you want to ride, then wash your head.” She did that, and Umm Ismāʿīl came to know of it, so she shaved her head. Then, when the following year came, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام reached that place, and Umm Ismāʿīl said to him, “What place is this?” He said to her, “This is the place in which Allah rendered your hajj of last year void.”

So this report contains an error by the narrator, and the matter became confused for him, because it is possible that he heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say to her, “Wash your head, and when you want to ride, wash your body,” but the narrator became confused and narrated it in reverse. What indicates that is that Hishām ibn Sālim, the narrator of this hadith, narrated what we have stated.
(371) 62. It was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in his tent while he was speaking to a woman, so I delayed. He said, “Come near. This is Umm Ismāʿīl. She has come, while I maintain that this is the place in which Allah rendered her hajj of last year void. I had intended to enter ihram, so I said: Put water for me in the tent. The slave-girl went with the water and placed it there. I found her light in my regard, so I had intercourse with her. Then I said: Wash your head and wipe it vigorously so that your mistress does not know of it. Then when you want to enter ihram, wash your body and do not wash your head, lest your mistress become suspicious. She then entered the tent of her mistress, and went to take something, and her mistress touched her head, and there was the stickiness of water. So she shaved her head and beat her. Then I said to her: This is the place in which Allah rendered your hajj void.”

(372) 63. As for the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Yamānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام did not see any problem in a person in janabah washing his head in the morning and washing the rest of his body at the time of salat." This does not indicate anything contrary to what we mentioned regarding the obligation of order; rather, it only indicates that continuity is not obligatory. According to us, continuity is not obligatory in ghusl; it is only obligatory in wudu, and discussion of that has already passed sufficiently, if Allah the Exalted wills. Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: And if he pours water using a vessel by which he seeks assistance, then let him do as we described, beginning with the head, then the right side of the body, then the left side. We have already clarified what that contains regarding the obligation of order. Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: Let him strive not to leave any part of the outward surface of his body except that the water touches it. This indicates that.

key_terms.اَلتَّرْتِيبِ: the required order in washing the parts of the body in ghusl
key_terms.اَلْإِحْرَامَ: the sacred state entered for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.اَلْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity caused by sexual intercourse or ejaculation
key_terms.اَلْمُوَالَاةَ: continuity between the acts of washing without interruption
key_terms.حَجَّكِ: your hajj, referring here to the pilgrimage whose validity is being discussed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith indicate about the order of washing in ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the rulings of ghusl from janabah and argues for the obligation of ترتيب, beginning with the head and then the sides of the body. It also reconciles an apparently problematic report by explaining a narrator’s confusion and distinguishes between the non-obligation of continuity in ghusl and the requirement that water reach the entire outward body.
